title: Echoes as Anchors: Probabilistic Costs and Attention Refocusing in LLM Reasoning
summary: Echoes as Anchors studies Echo of Prompt behavior in large reasoning models. It formalizes prompt echoes through probabilistic costs, analyzes attention refocusing, and introduces echo-distilled supervised fine-tuning and echoic prompting for improved math reasoning.
short_pitch: Large reasoning models often echo the original question before solving it. Echoes as Anchors shows that prompt echoes can act as cognitive anchors that refocus attention on the task, and formalizes this effect through Echo Likelihood Gap.
one_sentence_summary: Echoes as Anchors studies Echo of Prompt in large reasoning models, formalizes it with Echo Likelihood Gap, links it to attention refocusing, and uses Echo-Distilled SFT and Echoic Prompting to improve math reasoning.
canonical_framing: Echo of Prompt acts as a cognitive anchor for LLM reasoning, not merely redundant repetition. This is the paper's interpretation of its results, not a separately demonstrated claim.

evidence_scope.note: The paper's probabilistic and attention analyses are performed on a single model and a single benchmark. Do not quote these numbers without the model and benchmark attached.
evidence_scope.instrument: Echo presence is assigned by a two-layer MLP probe (test accuracy 0.912, AUROC 0.963, paper Table 7); roughly 9% detector error propagates into every group assignment.

evidence_highlights.claim: Echo of Prompt appears frequently in GSM8K reasoning traces.
evidence_highlights.scope: GSM8K; frequency measured by the MLP probe

evidence_highlights.claim: Correct traces show a higher Echo Likelihood Gap than wrong traces.
evidence_highlights.metric: 2.5231 vs. 2.4421 nats/token (difference +0.0811 against standard deviations near 0.78, i.e. a standardized effect around 0.10)
evidence_highlights.caveat: Small effect size. The paper also reports the suffix-only likelihood gap running the other way (wrong 1.2938 vs. correct 1.1449), read as echoes making locally coherent but flawed reasoning look more plausible.

evidence_highlights.claim: The Echo Likelihood Gap is a significant positive predictor of correctness.
evidence_highlights.metric: logistic regression on 1,319 GSM8K samples, beta = 0.24, p = 0.022, odds ratio 1.27 per nat/token
evidence_highlights.scope: DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B on GSM8K; echo length included as a covariate

evidence_highlights.claim: Correct traces route more attention to the echoed answer prefix than wrong traces, at every layer group.
evidence_highlights.metric: layers 7-18: 14.45% vs. 11.58% (+2.87 pp); last layer: 13.69% vs. 10.41% (+3.28 pp); all-layer mean: 10.64% vs. 8.49% (+2.15 pp). Discriminability AUC 0.716/0.719/0.723 and Cohen's d 0.820/0.832/0.828 for early/mid/late layer groups.
evidence_highlights.caveat: The layer-group effect sizes are close enough that mid-layer dominance describes where the raw gap peaks rather than a resolved localization. The raw gap is in fact largest at the last layer.

evidence_highlights.claim: The answer-to-question channel discriminates much more weakly than the answer-to-prefix channel.
evidence_highlights.metric: answer-to-question Cohen's d 0.482/0.303/0.184 by layer group vs. 0.820/0.832/0.828 for answer-to-prefix; layers 7-18 gap +0.66 pp vs. +2.87 pp
evidence_highlights.caveat: Not a null control. In the token-wise test, wrong traces attend significantly more to the question at 22 of 32 answer positions, while the answer-to-prefix difference is significant at 10 of 32. The finding is a shift of attention between two targets.

evidence_highlights.claim: The attention gap survives replacing the probe-estimated prefix with fixed prefix lengths.
Causal echo reinsertion improves previously failed reasoning traces in reasoning-tuned models but not in a base model.
evidence_highlights.metric: EM 15.85% -> 26.22% (+10.4 pts) DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B; 21.34% -> 29.27% (+7.9 pts) Qwen3-8B; null on Qwen3-8B-Base (10.56% -> 10.56%)
evidence_highlights.scope: GSM8K traces the model previously got wrong, truncated to 50% and resumed under identical questions, decoding parameters and seeds. Base rates are already conditioned on failure; these are not benchmark numbers.
evidence_highlights.caveat: No confidence intervals or repeated seeds are reported. The inserted text is a fixed template phrase ('now I need to look back at the question again:'), not a model-generated echo, so the experiment demonstrates that mid-trace re-grounding is causally effective rather than that the spontaneous echo is.

evidence_highlights.claim: Echo-Distilled SFT improves over normal SFT on most, but not all, reported cells.
evidence_highlights.metric: Qwen3-8B-Base: GSM8K +3.4, MathQA +11.8, Hendrycks-MATH +8.2. Qwen3-8B: +2.8 / +1.9 / +1.1. DeepSeek-Distill-Llama-8B: MathQA +3.4 and MATH +2.24, but GSM8K strict EM 78.2 vs. 80.5 for normal-SFT, a 2.3 point loss.
evidence_highlights.scope: Fine-tuned on 7k GSM8K samples with identical optimizer, schedule, batch size and steps; evaluated on GSM8K, MathQA and Hendrycks-MATH
evidence_highlights.caveat: Echo-bearing training sequences are longer (175 vs. 136 tokens on average), so the comparison is not token-matched.

evidence_highlights.claim: Traces that spontaneously contain an echo are more accurate than traces without one.
evidence_highlights.caveat: Descriptive comparison. Problems are not matched for difficulty, so this motivates the analysis rather than establishing an effect.

evidence_highlights.claim: Echoic Prompting outperformed thinking-token test-time scaling in the reported comparison.
evidence_highlights.metric: higher on AIME24 and MATH-500 than TTTS (Qian et al. 2025) under matched decoding and budgets
evidence_highlights.caveat: Reported as a figure with no numeric table, no error bars, and AIME24 contains only 30 problems. Directional evidence, not a general dominance result.

not_established: Neuron- or circuit-level mechanism. The evidence is attention- and behavior-level; 'mechanistic explanation' in the paper's contribution list should be read at that resolution.
Long-context behavior. Positional bias ('lost in the middle', Liu et al. 2024) appears in related work as motivation; all experiments are short math traces.
Generality beyond the 8B open-weight class, beyond mathematics, or beyond English prompts.
Why Echo of Prompt emerges. The paper leaves the origin of the behavior as an explicit hypothesis (appendix A.3).
A deployable correctness signal. The Echo Likelihood Gap is a population-level association with a small effect size, and the suffix-only result runs the other way.
primary_area: foundation or frontier models, including LLMs

faq_items.question: What is Echo of Prompt?
faq_items.answer: Echo of Prompt is the behavior where a large reasoning model repeats or rephrases the original user question inside its reasoning trajectory.

faq_items.question: What is Echo Likelihood Gap?
faq_items.answer: Echo Likelihood Gap is a probabilistic measurement used to quantify the cost and likelihood effect of prompt echoes in LLM reasoning.

faq_items.question: What is attention refocusing?
faq_items.answer: Attention refocusing is the mechanism-level observation that prompt echoes can shift attention back toward important problem or answer-prefix tokens during reasoning.

faq_items.question: What is Echoic Prompting?
faq_items.answer: Echoic Prompting is a training-free inference-time method that reintroduces the original question or a reminder during generation to re-ground reasoning.

faq_items.question: What is Echo-Distilled SFT?
faq_items.answer: Echo-Distilled SFT is supervised fine-tuning data preparation that encourages an echo-then-reason pattern.

research_areas.scope: attention- and behavior-level mechanism, not neuron- or circuit-level reverse engineering; all analysis on DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B and GSM8K
research_areas.evidence: layer-wise attention analysis over all 32 layers; MLP probe for echo detection (accuracy 0.912, AUROC 0.963); likelihood decomposition; causal echo reinsertion; answer-to-question attention as a weaker comparison channel

correct traces attend more to the echoed answer prefix at every layer group, with the raw gap peaking in mid-to-late layers (layers 7-18: 14.45% vs 11.58%); in the token-wise test wrong traces attend significantly more to the raw question at 22 of 32 positions while the answer-to-prefix difference is significant at 10 of 32; word-level heatmaps concentrate on key quantities; information-flow analysis shows echo tokens as an internal hub

research_areas.area: causal intervention on model-generated reasoning traces
research_areas.evidence: echo reinsertion into previously failed traces lifts exact match 15.85% -> 26.22% (+10.4 pts, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-Llama-8B) and 21.34% -> 29.27% (+7.9 pts, Qwen3-8B); null effect on non-reasoning Qwen3-8B-Base (10.56% -> 10.56%), which is what an anchoring account predicts and a more-tokens account does not

research_areas.scope: the EP comparison is a single model under greedy decoding
research_areas.evidence: EOP framed as a front-loaded, compute-shaping mechanism; Echoic Prompting scored higher than thinking-token test-time scaling (TTTS) on AIME24 and MATH-500 under matched decoding and budgets, reported as a figure without numeric tables or error bars

research_areas.scope: motivation, not result: all experiments are short math traces, echo prefixes average about 219 tokens
research_areas.evidence: the paper motivates the anchoring idea with positional-bias findings ('lost in the middle', Liu et al. 2024) and frames the echo as a self-generated re-injection of the problem statement; no long-context experiment is run
